obligations.summary: The notifying authority shall notify the Commission and other Member States of any relevant changes to the notification of a notified body via the electronic notification tool referred to in Article 30(2).
Extensions of the scope of a notification shall follow the procedures laid down in Articles 29 and 30, while other changes to the notification shall follow the procedures in Article 36(3)–(9).

Where a notified body decides to cease its conformity assessment activities, it shall inform the notifying authority and the providers concerned as soon as possible and, in the case of a planned cessation, at least one year before ceasing its activities.

Where a notified body ceases its activities, another notified body assuming responsibility must complete a full assessment of the affected high-risk AI systems before issuing new certificates within the nine-month transitional validity period.
exceptions: Certificates may remain valid for nine months after cessation if another notified body has confirmed in writing it will assume responsibilities for the high-risk AI systems covered by those certificates.

obligations.summary: Where a notified body has ceased its activity, the notifying authority shall withdraw the designation.

Where a notifying authority has sufficient reason to consider that a notified body no longer meets the requirements of Article 31 or is failing to fulfil its obligations, it shall without delay investigate the matter with the utmost diligence, inform the notified body of objections, allow it to make its views known, and then restrict, suspend or withdraw the designation as appropriate, immediately informing the Commission and other Member States.
Where its designation has been suspended, restricted, or fully or partially withdrawn, the notified body shall inform the providers concerned within 10 days.

In the event of restriction, suspension or withdrawal of a designation, the notifying authority shall take appropriate steps to ensure that the files of the notified body are kept and made available to notifying authorities in other Member States and to market surveillance authorities upon request.

In the event of restriction, suspension or withdrawal of a designation, the notifying authority shall assess the impact on certificates issued, submit a report to the Commission and Member States within three months, require the notified body to suspend or withdraw unduly issued certificates, inform the Commission and Member States of such certificates, and provide relevant information to the national competent authority of the Member State where the provider is registered.

Where a designation has been suspended or restricted (excluding unduly issued certificates), certificates shall remain valid if the notifying authority confirms within one month there is no risk and outlines a remediation timeline, or confirms no new certificates will be issued and addresses ongoing monitoring responsibilities; where the notified body cannot support existing certificates, the provider must confirm in writing within three months that another qualified notified body is temporarily assuming the monitoring functions.
exceptions: Certificates unduly issued are excluded from this validity provision.

obligations.summary: Where a designation has been withdrawn (excluding unduly issued certificates), certificates shall remain valid for nine months provided the national competent authority confirms no risk to health, safety or fundamental rights, and another notified body confirms in writing it will assume immediate responsibility and complete its assessment within 12 months; the national competent authority may extend provisional validity in three-month increments not exceeding 12 months total, and the authority or assuming notified body shall immediately inform the Commission, other Member States, and other notified bodies.
exceptions: Certificates unduly issued are excluded from this validity provision.
